issues.failure_explanation: Both gradient coefficients are positive only if c^*/(gamma c_*) < eps_4 < c_*/c^*, which requires 1/gamma < (c_*/c^*)^2. Since c_* <= c^*, this is strictly stronger than 1/gamma < 1, so the asserted chain is in general impossible. The analogous 1/gamma>1 case likewise needs 1/gamma > (c^*/c_*)^2. The ratio c_*/c^* depends on the stabilization, which the experiments vary over six orders of magnitude.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply Cauchy-Schwarz in the a_h^E semi-inner product, |a_h^E(psi,phi)| <= a_h^E(psi,psi)^{1/2} a_h^E(phi,phi)^{1/2}. Then use Young with eps in (1/gamma,1), or the analogue for 1/gamma>1, and only afterwards apply (a3.7)-(a3.8).
issues.overall_effect: As proved, discrete weak T-coercivity, and with it the stability of the discrete source problem, is established only in a stabilization-dependent sub-range of gamma rather than the full natural case.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement that k_h^2 (an eigenvalue of (a3.10) by definition) is not an eigenvalue of (a3.10) is self-contradictory. What is needed is that k^2 is not a discrete eigenvalue for small h, and the cited work treats a different problem. In finite dimensions the Fredholm alternative gives solvability for each fixed h but no h-independent bound. Weak T-coercivity with a Garding term does not yield the uniform inf-sup that (a3.11) requires.

issues.failure_explanation: A_h is defined with b, whereas (a3.5) and the computed eigenproblem (a3.3) use b_h. Under the b-definition, the eigenpairs of A_h solve a_h(U,Psi)=mu^{-1} b(U,Psi), not (a3.3), so the spectral theory controls the wrong lambda_{j,h}. Under a b_h-definition, A_h is not defined on W, because S_b needs point-value DoFs of f in L^2. Lemma 3.3 uses exactly such S_b terms. A_h^* uses b_h, so T_h^* is not the b-adjoint of T_h and the first identity in the proof of Theorem 3.1 fails.
